Package br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.domain.capture

Class Camera

java.lang.Object
br.edu.unipampa.varzinho.domain.capture.Camera
Direct Known Subclasses:
FixedCamera, PtzCamera, StreamCamera
public abstract class Camera extends Object
Equipment mounted on a court, recording continuously into its own buffer.

Its status decides whether footage is taken at all: a camera that is not recording accepts frames and drops them, so the buffer never holds seconds the camera was switched off for.

      protected Camera(String id, String model, Resolution resolution, int bufferSeconds)
      Builds a camera that is switched off, with an empty buffer of the given length.
      Parameters:
      id - the identifier, unique across the gym the camera is installed in
      model - the make and model of the equipment
      resolution - the resolution it records at
      bufferSeconds - how many of the most recent seconds the camera keeps
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the id or model is missing or blank, the resolution is missing, or the buffer is not at least one second long

  • Method Details

    • startRecording

      public void startRecording()
      Puts the camera to work, filling its buffer second by second.

      A camera that was not recording starts on an empty buffer: whatever it held from before belongs to a moment, or a court, it is no longer watching, and a highlight must never pass that off as the present. A camera already recording keeps going.

      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the camera is under maintenance — equipment on the bench is not on a court, and nothing but a technician takes it off

    • sendToMaintenance

      public void sendToMaintenance()
      Takes the camera to the bench, from whatever state it was in. It stops recording, and nothing but releaseFromMaintenance() brings it back.

    • releaseFromMaintenance

      public void releaseFromMaintenance()
      Brings the camera back from the bench switched off. It records again only once someone calls startRecording().
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the camera is not under maintenance

    • stopRecording

      public void stopRecording()
      Takes the camera off duty. What it already holds stays in the buffer, unreadable, until it is switched on again and starts afresh.
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if the camera is under maintenance — stopping it would silently report it as merely switched off

    • record

      public void record(Frame frame)
      Feeds one second of footage to the camera, which keeps it only while it is recording. A camera that is off drops what it is sent rather than refusing it: the gym goes on producing seconds whatever this camera is doing.
      Parameters:
      frame - the second that just went by

    • recordedWindow

      protected final List<Frame> recordedWindow(int seconds)
      The most recent window the camera holds, for a subclass to turn into a clip.

      Protected because the buffer is the camera's own memory: a court asks the camera for a capture, never for its frames.

      The refusal to read from a camera that is off lives here rather than in each subclass: a camera that stops recording keeps whatever it had, and handing that stale window out would pass off the past as the present. A subclass cannot forget a rule it never had to write.

      Parameters:
      seconds - how many of the most recent seconds to read
      Returns:
      the window, oldest first
      Throws:
      EmptyBufferException - if the camera is not recording, or has not recorded that many seconds yet

    • captureLastSeconds

      public abstract VideoClip captureLastSeconds(int seconds)
      Freezes the most recent seconds into a clip. Each kind of camera produces one its own way, and a court triggers them all through this single call.

      Every kind keeps one promise: the clip is finished when this returns. A kind that writes a file has written it, so whoever holds the clip may archive it at once, without knowing which kind of camera cut it.

      Parameters:
      seconds - how much of the recent past to keep
      Returns:
      the finished clip that stands for those seconds
      Throws:
      EmptyBufferException - if the camera is not recording, or has not recorded that many seconds yet

    • clipName

      protected final String clipName(Frame last)
      The start of a clip's file name, unique for this camera: the id, the second the window ends on, and how many clips the camera has cut so far. The count is what keeps two triggers ending on the same second from naming the same file.
      Parameters:
      last - the most recent frame of the window being frozen
      Returns:
      the file name without its extension, which the subclass adds

    • clipFrom

      protected final VideoClip clipFrom(String filePath, int seconds)
      Builds the clip for a window this camera has already taken, stamping it with what every camera knows about its own footage.

      The size is an estimate, not a measurement: no frame is ever encoded in Java, so megapixels times seconds is as close to the truth as this model gets. A stream camera's real file is written outside the domain, and its size is still estimated.

      Parameters:
      filePath - where the subclass decided the clip belongs
      seconds - the length of the window being frozen
      Returns:
      the clip, at this camera's resolution and with its estimated size
